findings.what: Two cases break lastok() and t7_trigger's header filter, since both only look for '[empty stdout'. (1) The poller writes '[ERROR <exception>]' notes, for example a 180 s TimeoutExpired, x3 with an empty body (lb_poll.py l.17). lastok treats that block as valid, returns an empty block, and T7 prints its header with no status. (2) A block whose header carries '[empty stdout' retry notes but whose body is valid is skipped. That happened in 3 of 571 historical blocks, which delays T7 by one cycle (~10 min) and makes lastok use 10-min-old data.
findings.evidence: experiments/lb_poll/lb_poll.py l.11-21; retry-then-success blocks 25 Sep 19:11:08Z, 27 Sep 17:43:34Z, 28 Sep 15:15:31Z; 0 '[ERROR' headers so far. Piped synthetic test: the current awk returns the empty [ERROR block and skips the valid mixed block; the body-based awk returns the 14:19:28Z block and the valid mixed block respectively.
findings.action:
Cheapest option, with no restart of the armed jobs: if T7 prints a header line with no 'SubmissionStatus' (or manual_admit reports odd output), read the newest poll.log block that contains a '^ref,' line by hand before coding T7/T8. Optional robust fix: lastok(){ awk '/^=== /{if (cur ~ /
ref,/) blk=cur; cur=""} {cur=cur"
"$0} END{if (cur ~ /
ref,/) blk=cur; print blk}' experiments/lb_poll/poll.log; }, and in t7_trigger take h=$(lastok | grep -m1 '^=== ' | cut -c5-24). Running jobs sourced lastok.sh at start, so editing the file changes nothing until t7_trigger.sh and manual_admit.sh are restarted. Given ~0.5% odds per block, prefer the manual rule over restarting armed jobs.
